title: Lecture 4: Selection, operators and encodings
outline:
Lecture 4 explainer (Nature-Inspired Computation, ECM3412, "Selection, operators and encodings"). 116 s, 11 scenes: title card 4 s, nine one-idea scenes of 10-13 s, recap 9 s. It follows the lecture order 4.1-4.9: how a genetic algorithm (GA) refreshes its population (generational vs steady-state, elitism, replace weakest vs replace first weaker), how it picks parents (selection pressure, roulette wheel, rank, tournament), how it makes children (mutation that fits the encoding, 1-point / 2-point / uniform crossover) and finally the EA lab (two complete algorithms evolving a 12x12 pixel heart). Everything is shown by pictures that build up; text is only short labels and the caption. Lecture 5 (already made) covers permutation encodings in depth, so Lecture 4 touches permutations in one row only.
VIDEO-WIDE COLOUR ROLES (keep them in every scene; names are the colour words of the app): grey = an ordinary individual, an unchanged gene, a neutral label; blue = the individual picked as a parent or the winner, the gene that changed, the evolving picture, parent 1 in the crossover scene; purple = a new child made by an operator, the operator tags, parent 2 in the crossover scene; green = the best, kept, valid, the target, the healthy outcome; red = the weakest / evicted, too strong (superfit), invalid, a wrong pixel, "too little / too much"; orange = attention: a scan cursor, drawn contestants, the original best in the takeover heatmap, a missing gene. Sticker look, no gradients, no white, labels >= 28 px, everything >= 12 px inside the stage (936 x 640), UK spelling.
LECTURE FACTS THE SCENES RELY ON (all numbers verified with code):
(4.1) Generational GA: selection plus operators build a completely new population each generation, the old one is discarded; without elitism the best fitness can go DOWN. An elitist generational GA copies the n best into the next generation unchanged, so the best is never lost. Steady-state GA: apply the operators only N times (N = 1 or 2) per step; the children replace weak members, everyone else stays; with replace-weakest it is automatically elitist. Lesson numbers: population [0.1, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.9]; a generational step gives [0.5, 0.3, 0.3, 0.7, 0.7] (best 0.9 lost, new best 0.7); a steady-state step puts a child of 0.5 in place of the weakest 0.1.
(4.2) Replace weakest: scan the whole population, evict the minimum (if the child is at least as good): greedy, high pressure, the best always survives. Replace first weaker: scan from the top, replace the first member weaker than the child, then stop: cheaper, weak members survive longer, more diversity. Example: slots [0.7, 0.8, 0.3, 0.9, 0.1], child 0.5: weakest -> slot 5 (0.1) after 5 looks giving [0.7, 0.8, 0.3, 0.9, 0.5]; first weaker -> slot 3 (0.3) after 3 looks giving [0.7, 0.8, 0.5, 0.9, 0.1].
(4.3) Selection pressure = how much more likely a fit individual is picked than an unfit one. Too little (random picks): drift, no progress. Too much (always pick the best): one individual's copies take over within a few generations, diversity vanishes, premature convergence. Modest, tunable pressure is the sweet spot (tournament size, rank bias). Takeover heatmap = selection only, no mutation or crossover, 12 individuals with fitness 1..12, seed 4: copies of the best (fitness 12) per generation 0..7: random [1,2,4,3,2,3,2,3], tournament t=2 [1,1,2,3,5,7,10,11], always best [1,12,12,12,12,12,12,12].
(4.4) Roulette: p_i = f_i / sum(f). Fitnesses 2, 3, 5 (total 10) -> 20%, 30%, 50%. Superfit: 100, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1 (total 101) -> 99.0%, 0.4%, 0.3%, 0.2%, 0.1%: the best takes over at once. (Roulette also depends on absolute values, and breaks for minimising or negative fitness; those two are not shown.)
(4.5) Rank: sort, the best gets rank P, the worst rank 1; p_i = rank_i / (P(P+1)/2). Same population 100, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1 -> ranks 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, sum 15 -> 33%, 27%, 20%, 13%, 7% (the superfit no longer takes 99%). Only the order matters. Bias knob rank^b: b=1 weights 5,4,3,2,1; b=2 weights 25,16,9,4,1 (sum 55) -> 45%, 29%, 16%, 7%, 2%; b=0 weights all 1 -> 20% each (random, no pressure).
(4.6) Tournament: choose t individuals at random WITH replacement, the fittest wins. Population fitness #1=3, #2=8, #3=5, #4=1, t=2: example draws #1 (3) and #3 (5), #3 wins, and the best (#2) was not even drawn. Win chance of the individual of rank r (1 = worst) in a population of P: (r/P)^t - ((r-1)/P)^t; best wins with 1 - (1-1/P)^t. For [#1..#4] = [3,8,5,1]: t=1 25/25/25/25; t=2 18.75/43.75/31.25/6.25; t=3 10.9/57.8/29.7/1.6; t=4 5.9/68.4/25.4/0.4 (percent). t=1 is random selection, bigger t = more pressure. It only compares, so no sorting and any fitness scale works.
(4.7) The encoding decides the mutation: binary = bit flip; integer (k-ary) = single-gene re-roll (352872 -> 312872, the 5 becomes a fresh value 1); real-valued = add small Gaussian noise (0.30, 0.20, 0.40 -> 0.30, 0.27, 0.40, +0.07); permutation = every city exactly once, so re-rolling one gene breaks it (DEGJA -> DEGDA: D twice, J missing) while swapping two genes keeps it valid (DEGJA -> DAGJE). Swap on integers can never create a value that is not already there (exploration).
(4.8) Crossover on P1 = ABCDEFGH, P2 = KLMNOPQR: 1-point cut after gene 5: child 1 ABCDEPQR, child 2 KLMNOFGH; 2-point cuts after genes 2 and 6: child 1 ABMNOPGH, child 2 KLCDEFQR; uniform mask 01001101 (1 = take that gene from the other parent): child 1 ALCDOPGR, child 2 KBMNEFQH. Crossover only recombines genes the parents already have; new values come from mutation.
(4.9) EA lab: a solution is a 12x12 black/white picture = 144 bits, fitness = fraction of pixels that match the target (the heart, 82 pixels on); 1.0 = perfect. Lecture algorithm 1 = steady-state, mutation only, tournament (t = 3), replace worst. Lecture algorithm 2 = generational, elitist (1 elite), rank-based selection, crossover (rate 0.8) plus mutation (1/144 per bit). Population 30. With seed 1 both start from the same random population (best 88/144); algorithm 1 reaches 144/144 after 3,069 evaluations and algorithm 2 after 4,844 (algorithm 1 is faster in all of seeds 1-10). Mutation is the only source of new genetic material.
SCRIPT ORDER OF THE PAGE videos/lecture-4.html: engine.js, cards.js, l5/common.js, l4/common.js, l4/common-2.js, scene files in order (like lecture-5.html; l6 is not needed).

titleCard.title: Selection & operators
titleCard.sub: Who gets to breed, and how children are made

title: Replace everyone,
or just a few
scenes.spec:
IDEA: how many individuals change per step. Reuse L4.tiles, L4.tag, L5.badge (valid: "best kept", invalid: "best lost", w 260, h 68).
DATA (compute with L4.generational / L4.replaceWeakest, assert the results): population [0.1, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.9] (best = last tile). Generational children [0.5, 0.3, 0.3, 0.7, 0.7] replace everyone -> best 0.9 lost. With 1 elite the 0.9 stays in slot 5 and slots 1-4 take the first four children [0.5, 0.3, 0.3, 0.7] -> row [0.5, 0.3, 0.3, 0.7, 0.9]. Steady-state: one child 0.5 replaces the weakest (0.1, slot 1) -> [0.5, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.9].
LAYOUT: two panels stacked. Panel A (generational): grey tag "generational" at (12, 66); badge at (12, 126); tile row at x 300, y 60, five 104 x 104 tiles, gap 14, font 52, grey with the 0.9 tile green; a small green tag "elite" under tile 5 (about y 182). Panel B (steady-state): grey tag "steady-state" at (12, 456); badge at (12, 516); tile row at x 300, y 450, same look; a purple child tile "0.5" (104 x 104) hovers above slot 1 at (300, 310).
TIMELINE: 0.6 tag A and the five tiles pop in (stagger 0.1). 1.8-3.4 the five tiles flip left to right (stagger 0.18, flip 0.5 s, small hop) into purple 0.5, 0.3, 0.3, 0.7, 0.7: the green best disappears. 3.5 badge "best lost" (red cross) pops. Hold. 5.0-5.9 flip everything back to the old values and tones (stagger 0.06), badge fades. 6.0 the "elite" tag pops under tile 5 and tile 5 bumps once; 6.3-7.6 tiles 1-4 flip to purple 0.5, 0.3, 0.3, 0.7 (stagger 0.15), tile 5 stays green and untouched; 7.7 badge "best kept" (green tick) pops. 8.6 panel B appears (tag, then tiles with stagger 0.08); 9.0 the purple child pops in above slot 1. 9.5 tile 1 (0.1) turns red and shakes. 10.0-10.5 the child drops onto slot 1; 10.4-10.8 slot 1 flips 0.1 -> 0.5 (purple) and the child tile disappears; the other four tiles never move or change. 10.9 badge "best kept" pops. Hold to the end.
CAPTIONS: [0.9, 4.6, "Generational: the whole population is replaced."], [5.2, 8.4, "Elitism copies the best across unchanged."], [8.8, 12.5, "Steady-state: one child replaces the weakest."].
FINAL STATE: A = [0.5, 0.3, 0.3, 0.7 purple, 0.9 green with "elite"] + "best kept"; B = [0.5 purple, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.9 green] + "best kept".

title: A child needs a slot:
who gets replaced?
scenes.spec:
IDEA: two ways to choose who a steady-state child evicts, run side by side. Reuse L4.tiles, L4.tag, L5.cross / L5.tick (+ L5.drawOn), L4.replaceWeakest, L4.replaceFirstWeaker.
DATA: slots [0.7, 0.8, 0.3, 0.9, 0.1] in both panels, child 0.5. Weakest: scans all 5 slots (5 looks), evicts slot 5 (0.1) -> [0.7, 0.8, 0.3, 0.9, 0.5]. First weaker: scans from slot 1, 0.7 and 0.8 are not weaker, 0.3 is: stops at slot 3 (3 looks) -> [0.7, 0.8, 0.5, 0.9, 0.1].
LAYOUT: tile rows at x 348 (five 96 x 96 tiles, gap 12, font 48): panel A at y 140, panel B at y 440. Left column (x 12): grey tag "replace weakest" at (12, 146) / "replace first weaker" at (12, 446); under each a grey tag counter at (12, row y + 66) reading "0 looks" -> "5 looks" / "3 looks". A purple child tile "0.5" (96 x 96) hovers above slot 1 of each panel (y row - 120).
TIMELINE: 0.5-1.4 both rows, tags and children pop in. 1.6 both panels start scanning at the same time: an orange cursor (the tile turns orange for 0.45 s, counter ticks up) steps slot 1 to 5 at 1.6, 2.05, 2.5, 2.95, 3.4. Panel B only: a slot that is NOT weaker (slots 1 and 2) gets a small grey cross drawn on below its tile (centre 26 px under the tile, size 32) as the cursor leaves it; panel A shows only the cursor and the counter. Panel B: the cursor reaches slot 3 at 2.5, the 0.3 gets a green tick below it and at 2.9 turns red: B has stopped, its counter freezes at "3 looks". Panel B child slides above slot 3 (3.0-3.5) and drops (3.5-4.0), slot 3 flips 0.3 -> 0.5 purple (3.9-4.3). Panel A keeps scanning until 3.85 (counter "5 looks"), then at 3.9 the lowest tile (0.1) turns red; its child slides to slot 5 (4.0-4.6), drops (4.6-5.1), slot 5 flips 0.1 -> 0.5 purple (5.0-5.4). 6.0 an orange tag "survives" pops under panel B's 0.1 tile (tile 5) with one bump. Hold.
CAPTIONS: [0.8, 2.4, "A child with fitness 0.5 arrives."], [2.6, 6.0, "First weaker stops early. Weakest checks all five."], [6.2, 9.5, "The 0.1 survives: more variety is kept."].
FINAL STATE: A [0.7, 0.8, 0.3, 0.9, 0.5 purple] "5 looks"; B [0.7, 0.8, 0.5 purple, 0.9, 0.1] "3 looks" with "survives" under the 0.1.

title: Too little: no progress
Too much: stuck early
scenes.spec:
IDEA: selection pressure is how fast the fit take over. Three heatmaps filled row by row at the same time: selection only, no mutation, no crossover. Reuse L4.heat, L4.tag, L4.takeoverRows.
DATA: rows = L4.takeoverRows(method, 4, 12, 8) for "random", "tournament" (t = 2) and "best": 12 individuals, 8 generations; all three share the same generation-0 row [6, 8, 7, 10, 5, 9, 11, 2, 1, 3, 4, 12] (fitness 12 is orange = the original best, other cells deeper green = fitter). Copies of the best per row: random [1,2,4,3,2,3,2,3], tournament [1,1,2,3,5,7,10,11], always best [1,12,12,12,12,12,12,12] (the scene shows these counts, taken from the matrices).
LAYOUT: three panels, x = 12, 336, 660, each cols 12 x cw 22 = 264 wide, 8 rows x ch 44 = 352 tall, heatmaps at y 70. Grey tags centred over each heatmap at y 12: "random", "tournament", "always best". Under each heatmap (y 444) an orange tag showing the best's share "1 / 12" that updates as rows appear. Verdict tags at y 520: red "too little" (left), green "modest" (middle), red "too much" (right).
TIMELINE: 0.5-1.2 the three framed empty heatmaps and tags pop in. 1.3 row 0 appears in all three. Rows 1-7 then appear one after the other at 1.9 + (row - 1) * 0.62 (row 7 at 6.2), the counters following. You see: random keeps shuffling, its orange never takes over and the colours do not get deeper; tournament deepens to green with orange creeping in over about 7 rows; always best turns solid orange at row 1 and nothing changes after. 7.0 / 7.3 / 7.6 the verdict tags pop (left, middle, right). Hold.
CAPTIONS: [1.0, 3.4, "Each row is a generation. Orange is the best."], [3.6, 6.8, "Only selection acts: no mutation, no crossover."], [7.2, 10.5, "Too little: no progress. Too much: stuck early."].
FINAL STATE: all 8 rows visible, counters 3 / 12, 11 / 12 and 12 / 12 in row 7, the three verdict tags shown.

title: Roulette: slices sized
by fitness
scenes.spec:
IDEA: the chance to be picked equals the slice, and a superfit slice swallows the wheel. Reuse L4.wheel, L4.bar, L4.tiles (single chips), L4.tag, L4.pct, L4.rouletteProbs, L4.spinTo, L4.pickSlice.
DATA: wheel 1 = fitnesses [2, 3, 5] (total 10) -> 20%, 30%, 50% (angles 72, 108, 180 degrees). Spins: u = 7.3 lands in the 5-slice (C), u = 3.4 in the 3-slice (B). Wheel 2 = [100, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1] (total 101): 99% (100/101 = 99.0%), 0.4%, 0.3%, 0.2%, 0.1%; spins u = 61.0 and 12.4 both land in the 100 slice. Rotations from L4.spinTo, never typed.
LAYOUT: wheel at cx 250, cy 350, r 190, pointer fixed above it. Grey slices (alternating neutral shades) carry their fitness number (28 px or more) in ink. Under the wheel a grey tag at (center 250, y 574): "2 + 3 + 5 = 10". Right column x 520-924: one row per individual, pitch 78 from y 150: a chip (L4.tiles, 96 x 60, font 34) with the fitness, a horizontal L4.bar (x 630, len 200, thick 28) and the percent text in the fixed column at x 840 (34 px).
TIMELINE: 0.5 wheel frame and pointer pop in. 1.2-3.0 the three slices sweep in one after another (0.5 s each) with their numbers, and their chips + bars grow to 20%, 30%, 50% in step; 2.8 the sum tag pops. 3.4-4.8 spin 1 (ease-out, 2 full turns): lands on the 5-slice, which pops out 12 px and turns blue, its bar and chip turn blue. 5.0-6.4 spin 2 lands on the 3-slice (the 5-slice settles back first). 6.7-8.2 the wheel morphs (p interpolated from [.2,.3,.5,0,0] to [.990,.004,.003,.002,.001]): the first slice swells to nearly the whole wheel and turns red, chips flip to 100, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1, two more rows pop in, bars and numbers follow ("99%" in red), the sum tag changes to "total 101". 8.4-9.6 spin 3 (u = 61.0) lands in the red slice, 9.9-10.9 spin 4 (u = 12.4) lands there too: each time the red slice pops out. Hold.
CAPTIONS: [0.8, 3.2, "Each slice is sized by fitness."], [3.4, 6.4, "The bigger the slice, the likelier the pick."], [6.8, 9.4, "One superfit individual takes 99% of the wheel."], [9.6, 11.5, "It is picked again and again."].
FINAL STATE: the five-slice superfit wheel, red 99% slice popped out, bars 99%, 0.4%, 0.3%, 0.2%, 0.1% (grey slivers). Scene 6 starts from this same population.

title: Rank selection ignores
the raw numbers
scenes.spec:
IDEA: replace fitness by its position in the sort, then add a pressure knob. Same population as the end of scene 5. Reuse L4.tiles (chips), L4.bar, L4.knob, L4.tag, L4.rouletteProbs, L4.rankProbs, L4.pct.
DATA: fitness [100, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1] -> roulette p = 99%, 0.4%, 0.3%, 0.2%, 0.1% (grey start); ranks [5, 4, 3, 2, 1] (sum 15) -> rank p = 33%, 27%, 20%, 13%, 7%. Knob b (rank^b): b=1 weights 5,4,3,2,1; b=2 weights 25,16,9,4,1 (sum 55) -> 45%, 29%, 16%, 7%, 2%; b=0 weights 1,1,1,1,1 -> 20% each. Compute every bar and number with L4.rankProbs, interpolating b while the thumb moves.
LAYOUT (five rows, pitch 84, first row y 84, row height 64): column headers (plain dim 28 px text, no pill) at y 20: "fitness" (x 12), "rank" (x 182), "chance" (x 322). Fitness chips x 12 (130 x 64, font 36; the 100 chip red, the rest grey). Rank chips x 182 (100 x 64, purple). Bars x 322, len 400, thick 36; percent text column at x 740 (34 px). A grey tag "total 15" at (740, 12). Knob (L4.knob, stops 0, 1, 2) at x 250, y 560, w 400, pill "b = 1" at x 100.
TIMELINE: 0.5-1.4 headers and the five fitness chips pop in. 1.6-2.6 grey roulette bars grow: the 100 row's bar fills 99% (red, "99%"), the others are slivers ("0.4%", "0.3%", "0.2%", "0.1%"). 3.4-4.4 rank chips 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 pop in (stagger 0.2) and the "total 15" tag pops. 4.8-6.2 every bar morphs to the rank chance and turns green (33%, 27%, 20%, 13%, 7%); a dashed ghost marker stays at the old 99% end of the first bar. 7.0 the knob row appears with the thumb at b = 1. 7.6-8.6 thumb to b = 2, bars morph to 45/29/16/7/2; at 8.6-9.0 the rank chips flip to the weights 25, 16, 9, 4, 1 and the header "rank" becomes "weight". 9.2-10.0 thumb to b = 0, bars morph to 20% each, chips flip to 1, 1, 1, 1, 1 (10.0-10.3). The pill text follows (when the thumb is between stops show the nearest whole value).
CAPTIONS: [0.8, 3.2, "Roulette: the superfit takes 99%."], [3.4, 6.8, "Rank: only the order counts, not the gaps."], [7.2, 10.5, "The exponent b turns the pressure up or down."].
FINAL STATE: b = 0, five equal green 20% bars, weights 1, the ghost marker still on the first bar.

title: Tournament: draw t,
the best wins
scenes.spec:
IDEA: pick t individuals at random and keep the fittest; bigger t = tougher competition. Reuse L4.tiles, L4.bar (dir "v"), L4.knob, L4.tag, L5.dice, L5.cross / L5.tick, L4.tournProbs, L4.pct.
DATA: four individuals #1..#4 with fitness [3, 8, 5, 1]. Example (lesson): the two draws are #1 (3) and #3 (5) -> #3 wins; the best (#2 = 8) was not drawn. Win chances from L4.tournProbs([3,8,5,1], t) in tile order: t=1 25/25/25/25; t=2 19/44/31/6 (18.75, 43.75, 31.25, 6.25); t=3 11/58/30/2 (10.94, 57.81, 29.69, 1.56); t=4 6/68/25/0.4 (5.86, 68.36, 25.39, 0.39). (Cross-check by brute force over all P^t draws.)
LAYOUT: four tiles 120 x 120 (gap 36, font 64) at x 174, y 90, grey, with grey "#1".."#4" labels (28 px) at y 224. Two L5.dice (size 56) travel at y 12-70. Under the labels (y 270) tags appear: blue "parent" under #3, orange "not drawn" under #2. Phase 2: four vertical L4.bar (thick 90, len 190 px standing for 70%, so k = p / 0.7; baseline y 520, text above) aligned under the tiles, green. Knob (L4.knob, stops 1, 2, 3, 4) at x 250, y 580, w 440, pill "t = 1" at x 100.
TIMELINE: 0.5-1.3 tiles and labels pop in. 1.5-2.1 die 1 hops over tile #1 and it turns orange; 2.3-2.9 die 2 hops over tile #3, which turns orange (draws are independent: the same tile could be drawn twice). 3.2-3.8 the orange pair is compared: #1 (3) greys out with a cross, #3 (5) turns blue and pops, the "parent" tag appears; 4.0 the "not drawn" tag pops under #2. 5.0 dice and tags vanish, tiles back to grey; the knob and four 25% green bars appear (t = 1: pure random). 5.8-6.4 thumb to t = 2, bars morph to 19/44/31/6; 7.4-8.0 t = 3: 11/58/30/2; 9.0-9.6 t = 4: 6/68/25/0.4 (show "0.4%" for the 0.39%). Each state holds about 1 s.
CAPTIONS: [0.9, 3.6, "Draw two at random. The better one wins."], [3.8, 5.2, "The best was not even drawn."], [5.4, 7.6, "A bigger t means tougher competition."], [7.8, 10.5, "The best wins more often as t grows."].
FINAL STATE: t = 4, bars 6%, 68%, 25%, 0.4%, knob thumb on 4.

title: Mutation must fit
the encoding
scenes.spec:
IDEA: each encoding has its own sensible mutation, and the wrong one breaks a permutation. Four rows. Reuse L4.tiles, L4.tag, L4.bell, L5.dice, L5.badge (defaults "valid tour" / "not a tour"), L5.swapAt, L5.dupIdx, L5.missingOf, L5.isPerm.
DATA (genes counted from 1 below): binary 1 0 1 1 0 1, flip gene 3 -> 1 0 0 1 0 1; integer 3 5 2 8 7 2, re-roll gene 2 (5 -> 1, a value that was not there) -> 3 1 2 8 7 2; real 0.30 0.20 0.40, gene 2 plus 0.07 -> 0.27; tour D E G J A, re-roll gene 4 (J -> D) -> D E G D A (L5.dupIdx = genes 1 and 4, D twice, J missing, not a permutation), swap genes 2 and 5 (E and A) -> D A G J E (L5.swapAt(s, 1, 4), a permutation).
LAYOUT: tile rows at x 200, tile height 80, at y 14 (binary), 154 (integer), 294 (real), 434 (tour). Grey left tags at x 12, each 17 px below its tile row top: "binary", "integer", "real", "tour". Binary and integer: six 80 x 80 tiles gap 10, font 44; real: three 120 x 80 tiles gap 12, font 40; tour: five 80 x 80 tiles gap 10. Purple operator tags in the right column at x 772: "bit flip", "re-roll", "nudge", then on the tour row "re-roll" and later "swap". Decorations: a dice (size 44) just above the re-rolled gene (rows 2 and 4), the small bell curve (about 120 x 40) just above the nudged gene, a blue "+0.07" tag at x 604 on the real row, a dashed orange ghost tile "J" at slot 6 of the tour row. The L5.badge sits at (200, 536).
TIMELINE: 0.5-1.3 the first three rows pop in (grey). Row 1: 1.5 tag "bit flip"; 1.6-2.1 gene 3 turns blue and flips 1 -> 0; 2.3 the other genes turn green (valid), the changed gene stays blue. Row 2: 2.6 tag "re-roll" and a die above gene 2; 2.8-3.3 gene 2 flips 5 -> 1 (blue); 3.5 the rest turn green. Row 3: 3.8 tag "nudge", the bell curve draws on above gene 2 with its dot; 4.0-4.5 gene 2 flips 0.20 -> 0.27 and "+0.07" pops; 4.7 the rest turn green. Row 4: 5.0 the tour row pops in (grey) with the purple tag "re-roll" and a die above gene 4; 5.9-6.4 gene 4 flips J -> D; both D tiles (genes 1 and 4) turn red and shake, the orange ghost "J" appears after the row (missing), 6.5 badge "not a tour" pops. 7.8-8.3 gene 4 flips back to J, ghost and badge vanish. 8.5 the tag changes to "swap"; 8.7-9.5 genes 2 (E) and 5 (A) hop past each other (purple while moving) and land blue; the other tiles turn green; 9.6 badge "valid tour" pops. Hold.
CAPTIONS: [0.8, 4.8, "Each encoding needs its own kind of mutation."], [5.0, 7.8, "Re-rolling a tour breaks it: D twice, J lost."], [8.4, 11.5, "Swapping two genes keeps every city once."].
FINAL STATE: rows 1-3 green with one blue gene each, row 4 = D A G J E green with two blue genes and the badge "valid tour".

title: Crossover mixes
two parents' genes
scenes.spec:
IDEA: three ways to cut two parents and mix them, shown on the same strings. Reuse L4.tiles, L4.tag, L4.cutLine, L4.crossMask, L4.cross.
DATA: P1 = ABCDEFGH (blue tiles), P2 = KLMNOPQR (purple tiles). 1-point cut after 5: child 1 ABCDEPQR, child 2 KLMNOFGH. 2-point cuts after 2 and 6: child 1 ABMNOPGH, child 2 KLCDEFQR. Uniform mask 01001101: child 1 ALCDOPGR, child 2 KBMNEFQH. Each child tile has the colour of the parent it came from. Compute with L4.crossMask / L4.cross and assert.
LAYOUT: tile rows at x 200, 72 x 72 tiles gap 8 (pitch 80, font 40): P1 y 20, P2 y 108, mask row y 214 (appears in phase 3), child 1 y 330, child 2 y 418. Grey tags at x 12 ("parent 1" blue, "parent 2" purple, "mask", "child 1", "child 2" grey). The operator tag (purple, solid) at (200, 524) reads "1-point", then "2-point", then "uniform". The orange L4.cutLine runs from y 12 to 500 in the gap after gene k (x = 200 + 80 k - 4).

CAPTIONS: [1.4, 5.4, "One cut: swap the tails."], [5.8, 8.0, "Two cuts: swap the middle part."], [8.6, 11.5, "Uniform: a 1 in the mask swaps that gene."].

title: Put it together:
evolve a picture
scenes.spec:
IDEA: the lab's two lecture algorithms race to copy a pixel picture; fitness = pixels that match. Reuse L4.pixels, L4.tag, L5.tick / L5.drawOn (a tick disc beside each finished counter), L4.evolveLab, L4.HEART.
DATA: target = L4.HEART (12 x 12, 82 ones). a = L4.evolveLab("ss", 1), b = L4.evolveLab("gen", 1) (computed once in build()). Shared evaluation counter e(t) = 4844 * ramp(t, 1.6, 9.0, linear), displayed as max(30, round(e)). Each grid shows a.at(e) / b.at(e).bits with its fit "N / 144" (both start at 88 / 144, the same random best of 30). Algorithm 1 finishes at 3,069 evaluations (about 6.3 s), algorithm 2 at 4,844 (9.0 s).
LAYOUT: centre column: green tag "target" centred on x 468 at y 12, the target heart (L4.pixels, cell 14 = 168 px, green) at x 384, y 66; under it a grey tag "evals 30" counting up (centred, y 250). Left panel at x 48: blue tag "algorithm 1" at y 12, evolving picture at (48, 66) (cell 22 = 264 px, blue, wrong pixels outlined red), big match counter "88 / 144" (44 px, ink, centred under the picture) at y 338, an empty slot at y 398 for the finish tag, three stacked grey recipe tags at y 458, 510, 562: "steady-state", "tournament", "mutation". Right panel mirrored at x 624: "algorithm 2", recipe tags "generational", "rank", "crossover".
TIMELINE: 0.5-1.4 target, both pictures (noisy, red outlines everywhere) and tags pop in. 1.6-9.0 evolution time-lapse driven by e(t): counters tick, red outlines vanish, the heart emerges. Algorithm 1 completes at 6.3: its pixels turn green, a green tick pops, its counter reads "144 / 144" in green and a green tag "3,069 evaluations" pops into the slot at y 398; the shared evals counter keeps running. Algorithm 2 completes at 9.0: same, with "4,844 evaluations". Hold.
CAPTIONS: [0.8, 3.4, "Fitness: how many pixels match the heart."], [3.6, 6.0, "Two recipes race to copy it."], [6.6, 10.5, "Algorithm 1 got there first, in this run."].
FINAL STATE: both pictures are the green target heart with ticks, evaluation tags 3,069 and 4,844.

recap.spec:
Custom bare scene in the style of videos/l5/scene-10-recap.js (not VID.recapCard, because each point has an animated pictogram). Kicker "RECAP", head "Remember" (76 px) at the top left, Sprout (mood "love", size 150) at the top right. Three sticker cards (x 72, width 936, height 180, tops 240 / 444 / 648, tones blue, green, purple) slide in at 0.8 / 1.8 / 2.8 s; each has a 340 x 140 pictogram area at the left of the card (drawn at 340 x 140, shown 10% larger as in video 5) and a bold 42 px label at x 400 on two lines. Bottom row (y 904): one solid blue tag "Beat the Lecture 4 boss quiz" (34 px) pops in at 5.2 s. The pictograms loop; all motion is a function of t.
1. BLUE, label "Replace all," / "or just a few": five small tiles (48 px, no text, grey, the fifth green). Loop of 5.2 s starting at 1.4: all five flip left to right into purple (wave), hold, flip back; then only tile 1 turns red and flips to purple, hold, back.
2. GREEN, label "Tune the selection" / "pressure": five vertical bars (width 22, gap 10, green) showing L4.rankProbs([5, 4, 3, 2, 1], b).p with exponent b, and a small knob track beside them; loop of 4.8 s: b goes 1 -> 2 -> 0 -> 1, the bars morph (steep, then flat) with the thumb.
3. PURPLE, label "Operators fit" / "the encoding": tiles D E G J A (48 px, blue, letters 28 px). Loop of 6.4 s: re-roll the fourth gene J -> D (two D tiles turn red, red cross disc), flip back, then E and A hop past each other (purple while moving), tiles turn green and a green tick disc pops (L5.tick / L5.cross on a disc as in video 5).
Numbers in the bars come from L4.rankProbs. Nothing is typed; keep >= 12 px margins.
